subject: Performance qualification: latency buckets & context bounds
messages:

To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@lumina.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Performance qualification: latency buckets & context bounds

Jordan / Kai — great call this morning, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we keep momentum on the POC.

Key takeaways from today
- Latency target: 95th percentile <= 220ms for short queries (~256 tokens output) and <= 450ms for long streams (input+output ~8k tokens)
- Concurrency: initial load is 40 concurrent users with bursts to 120; sustained throughput target 500 TPS for embeddings route (separate) and 180 TPS for chat/generation during peak business hours
- Streaming requirement: user-facing streaming for long responses (token-by-token), with ability to fall back to non-streamed chunked responses for degraded states
- Context window: typical user request = 1k input tokens, expected long form = 6–8k input tokens; combined IO cap ~10k tokens realistic upper bound

Open questions we promised to validate
1) Latency sensitivity: how often do you need sub-250ms responses vs acceptable 400–500ms?
2) Worst-case concurrency pattern (all users starting long-form generation simultaneously?)
3) Any retention/compliance constraints that force private deployment?

We attached a short perf summary and a blank mutual action plan. Proposed immediate next steps
- Rishi: run a quick mapping of your 10k token IO profile into our latency buckets and send back estimated p95 numbers by EOD tomorrow (we'll attach the assumption table).
- Jordan/Kai: share a sample long-form prompt + typical conversation turns (anonymized) so we can simulate KV cache behavior.
- Monica: I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up to review the numbers and agree on canary thresholds.

Thanks — Hannah

--

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@lumina.ai>

Subject: Re: Performance qualification: latency buckets & context bounds

Thanks for the clear notes, Hannah. A few clarifications from our side:
- Sub-250ms is nice-to-have for quick lookups (search-like queries) but core UX is tolerant up to ~350ms for short answers. Long-form can accept 400–600ms per chunk if streaming keeps perceived latency low.
- Concurrency: our backend will typically fan-out requests when large cohorts are onboarded, so the 120 burst is realistic. We can stage ramping to 500 concurrent in later phases but want to qualify P95 at 120 first.
- Compliance: we need SOC2 and a simple data retention control; private deployment is not mandatory immediately but may be required by Q4.

I'll drop two anonymized examples (one short, one long) into the shared Drive link by lunchtime. For the KV cache sim, expect repeated context overlap across sessions ~30–40%.

Jordan

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-07-05T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance qualification: latency buckets & context bounds

Hannah — ran a quick mapping against our internal perf model this morning. Notes below (high-level assumptions attached in perf-metrics.csv):

Assumptions
- Model: open-quantized 13B variant (production-sim).
- HW: A100 equivalent, batching up to 8 tokens across 32 concurrent micro-batches for generation path, streaming enabled with 256-token chunking.
- KV cache hits: 35% reduces effective decode cost by ~20% on average.

Estimated p95 latency (approx)
- Short queries (256 tokens out): 210–260ms p95 depending on burst factor (single-request path; cold-start adds ~80ms)
- Long streaming (8k IO split into 256-token chunks): initial chunk 480–560ms, steady-state chunks 140–220ms p95; overall perceived latency acceptable if first chunk <=600ms and steady-state <250ms

Implications and mitigations
- We should define two latency buckets in the MAP: "lookup" (p95 <=350ms) and "long-form" (initial chunk p95 <=600ms; steady-state p95 <=250ms).
- For high burst concurrency, prefer smaller per-request batching and enforced token caps for long-form paths to protect tail latency.
- Fallback: non-streamed chunked responses or degrade to a smaller model variant when GPU queue length > threshold.

I'll upload the CSV with the scenario numbers and a short runbook for canary thresholds. Recommend we review with Lumina tomorrow at 10am PT.

-rishi
Principal Engineer, Redwood Inference

Jordan / Kai — thanks, Rishi — great ops-level guidance. Finalized asks and proposed MAP items for the demo canary:

1) Redwood to deliver:
- A perf runbook with the two latency buckets and measurable canary thresholds (attached: perf-metrics.csv)
- Canary config: 10% traffic -> 120 concurrent cap, streaming on, token cap 10k IO; fallback to smaller model at queue threshold = 30
- A short report after 24h canary with p50/p90/p95 for initial and steady-state chunks

2) Lumina to deliver before the canary:
- Two anonymized prompt sets (short + long) uploaded to the shared Drive link (Jordan)
- Expected concurrency patterns for a three-hour peak window (hourly breakdown)

3) Both parties: agree on fallbacks and escalation path (DocuSign sign-off for adding Dedicated if canary fails SLA)

I'll schedule the 30-min follow-up (tomorrow 10am PT) and a 24-hour canary window for the week after. If this plan looks good I'll convert the MAP to the shared mutual-action-plan.docx and send for signatures.

Best — Hannah
